biggest_gap.what: The questionnaire — RI-CHR01 §4 Route C, RI-JRN01 O9's mandatory route — reaches the player with neither its questions nor its answer. (a) buildCensusModel() at game/src/character/scene.js:267 sets `line: state.line` and never reads `state.question.text`, so all ten dilemma nodes draw one identical stock transition line above four unattached answers: 10 distinct question texts in the model, 1 distinct drawn line, 0 of 10 reaching the frame. (b) Across 240 runs covering all 10 races x 4 upbringings x 8 answer permutations with a verified even answer histogram (600 each of a/b/c/d), the route produced a named class 0 times out of 14, against RI-CHR01's pass floor of >= 6 and its 0-band of < 6.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: A player taking the route this game's opening is built around is shown forty answers to questions that are never asked, and is never once told what profession they turned out to be — the moment the route exists for does not occur in any configuration.

remedy.action: 1) In buildCensusModel(), when state.input.kind === 'questionnaire', set line: state.question.text and move the scribe's transition line to the aside slot (or to the writ.class-routes answer). The model already carries the text; this is one line. 2) In character/questionnaire.js's scoreAnswers, make the named-class match reachable: compare the resulting 3-primary/2-secondary skill set against classes.json's fourteen with a tolerance (>= 3 of 5 shared skills plus a matching family) rather than requiring an exact set — census.js already has on_match_named_class and %ClassName wired for the moment it succeeds. 3) In CensusSurface.sync(), filter a pick node's options against attributes already taken by earlier pick nodes so writ.class-custom-neglected cannot offer a favoured attribute, and wrap _censusApplyPending() so a refused answer can never throw out of the frame step.
remedy.acceptance: getCensusState().surface.rendered_text contains getCensusState().question.text at 10 of 10 questionnaire nodes and the 10 nodes yield 10 distinct drawn lines; a 240-run sweep over all 10 races x 4 upbringings with an even a/b/c/d answer histogram reaches >= 6 distinct named class_id values (>= 10 for the item's 10 band) and the Warden-Scribe's on_match_named_class line fires on every named match; and the full custom-class route completes on gamepad alone with 0 exceptions out of stepFrames.

secondary_observations.what: greetings.json's 300 cells / 1,500 lines have no world-side consumer. chData.greetings is written at game/src/engine.js:3706 and that is the only occurrence of 'greetings' in game/src/**. playerRaceClass() is called only from getReaction() (a harness oracle) and tools/analysis/creation-audit.mjs. No harness verb matches /greet/.

The 96 race-gated topic records are never evaluated: at helstrom-market every NPC's topic list is byte-identical for a Dunmer and a Saxhleel. sim/npc.js copies spec.topics verbatim and nothing filters on requires.race / forbids.race.

In the live raid encounter the party's swings whiff at resolve-frame separations of 0.60-1.14 m and connect only at 1.14-1.38 m, with lateral offset ~0 — an effective minimum reaching distance of ~1.14 m against S26's <= 0.35 m acceptance. The Saxhleel run is 12 attack_start / 12 WHIFF / 0 HIT and the party dealt zero damage in 730 frames of contact. The mechanism is this piece's own: engageMember() returns early while b.move is set, so a committed attacker cannot back off and its own root motion carries it from min_standoff_m 1.45 to 0.6-0.9 m during the active frames. tools/harness/cmb-reach.mjs --enemy inf_trash reports ACCEPTANCE FAIL on all seven turtle stand distances (0.287-0.341 of max HP vs 0.40 required); the tool ships in this tree, takes an --enemy flag, and was not run. The builder's attribution to 'a W1-09 resolver interaction' is honest about the symptom but wrong about the ownership.

A merchant's own derived disposition never reaches their prices: priceQuote() defaults `disposition` to 50 and no call site passes the live value, so a Deep-Kin seller at disposition 6 quotes as though at 50. This is the build's (defensible) resolution of the §4b double-application, and it costs RI-PRG05's 'read by the shop' requirement.
The guard law-factor and suspicion tables are still oracles: stepNPCs' `post` behaviour counts loiter_frames race-blind and nothing reads suspicionMultiplier.

No title surface exists (RI-JRN01 O1/O3, M3), unchanged from round 1; readWrit() is still not an object in the world and the stamped node draws no text at all; text entry drops characters (BJORN typed on a real keyboard produced 'bjon'); and neither NPC animates beyond a yaw turn across all 19 nodes.

greetings.json is a declared combinatorial expansion of 360 authored fragments and it meets RI-CHR02 §4c's intent rather than padding it: all 300 stances are distinct authored prose in the item's register, 1,400 of 1,500 output lines are distinct, distinct lines per (group, band) across the five player-race classes run 5 to 25 with the only 5 being RG-COURT (all-zero row, correctly identical), and a small authored set recombined at runtime is precisely the shape of Morrowind's own greeting table. What IS chargeable is that every §4c floor is met with 0-7% headroom against the 10 band's >= 20%, which puts the volume axis at 6 before consumption is considered at all.

arbitration_questions.question: RI-PRG05's buy_mult already contains -0.0060 x Disposition, and RI-CHR02 §4a puts the race term inside Disposition; §4b then applies a raceSurcharge of 1.00 - 0.006 x r on top, with the identical coefficient. Race is counted twice at the same weight. Which term owns it?
arbitration_questions.souls_side: Not a Souls concern; pricing is outside the fight.
arbitration_questions.morrowind_side: Morrowind owns the economy and disposition-affected prices. Either the surcharge is folded into the disposition term, or the disposition term is computed race-blind for pricing. The build chose the latter by hard-coding disposition 50, which costs RI-PRG05's requirement that disposition be read by the shop.

arbitration_questions.question: RI-CHR02 method 7 asserts quotes 'within 3% of {54, 70, 76} gold' at base 60, but those figures are the §4b surcharge multipliers alone. A real untrained quote is 60 x 1.2085 x 1.264 = 92 g. Is the method's table the surcharge or the quote?
arbitration_questions.morrowind_side: The method text should read 'surcharge multiplier', not 'quoted price'. The build ships both, correctly labelled (buy_surcharge_only 76, buy 92), which is the right way to hold a disputed bar.
arbitration_questions.proposed_seam_id: none — an item-text correction, not a seam

arbitration_questions.question: AR-2 B5 makes any soul-denominated price an automatic fail (S15), while RI-CHR03 §5 prices the birthsign re-cut at 'all souls currently carried, to a minimum of 25,000'. Still data-only; it will collide when the re-cut is built.
arbitration_questions.souls_side: S15: souls level you and only level you.
arbitration_questions.morrowind_side: RI-CHR03 §5 and RI-CHR01 §7 both prescribe the soul price as the thing that makes the re-cut non-routine.

Build churn: another builder's in-flight quest data made the tree unbootable partway through (QuestBook: 9 integrity failures in game/data/quests/**, from magic-utility.json, unrelated to W1-07); retried twice, then ran the remaining probe in a clean worktree at the same commit.
